h: Fly across the Thames after you've finished flying
p: The beauty of bouncing at The O2 is that the journey there and back can be half the adventure. Right beside the peninsula, the cable car glides across the Thames to the Royal Docks, giving you a cracking view over the river, Canary Wharf and the city skyline. It's a brilliant way to round off a session, especially for kids who've never seen London from up high. You can also hop on a river bus from North Greenwich Pier and sail back towards central London instead of heading underground.

A quick word on timing: when there's a big concert or event at the arena, the area and the Jubilee line get very busy in the run-up to show time. If you're planning a family visit, it's worth checking what's on that evening and aiming to be done and away before the crowds roll in. Weekday daytime sessions in the school holidays can be a calmer option too.

If you've got a full day, combine the bounce with Greenwich proper. The Cutty Sark is a famous tea clipper you can explore, the National Maritime Museum is free and packed with ships and stories, and up the hill at the Royal Observatory you can stand on the Prime Meridian. Greenwich Park's views back over the river are some of the best in London, and the climb up is a sneaky extra workout for anyone whose legs are still twitching from the trampolines.
